findings.summary: Active profile references cannot resolve to supplied profile records or definitions inside the declared bundle scope.
findings.adversarial_construction: Construct a schema-valid verifier bundle whose active extension registry reference has record_type PROFILE, while the inventory contains no PROFILE entry and the reference contains no content.
findings.consequence: BND-005 and all profile-dependent admission rules require an unstated profile store or fail without evaluating the declared contract.

findings.summary: Generic bundle content is selected by schema identifiers, but no schema-contract registry or supplied structural contract is part of the validation scope.
findings.adversarial_construction: Supply arbitrary content with a valid-looking schema_id/version and ask BND-004 or LIN-009 to decide structural validity without an in-scope contract.
findings.consequence: RESOLVED versus STRUCTURALLY_INVALID depends on an implementation-local registry or ambient repository, defeating self-contained verification.

findings.summary: Role visibility field rules accept producer and consumer role strings not constrained to the declared role set.
findings.adversarial_construction: Add an undeclared consumer role to a field rule and evaluate VIS-001 under two implementations, one rejecting it and one treating it as a new role.
findings.consequence: Condition privacy and arm visibility can diverge between conforming implementations.

findings.summary: Scenario-ID opacity is represented as a self-attested condition rather than a deterministic control against expected-result side channels.
findings.adversarial_construction: Encode the expected outcome in a schema-valid scenario identifier or fixture label while retaining scenario_identifiers_opaque_to_expected_result=true.
findings.consequence: A system under test may receive the scientific answer through metadata without any schema failure.

findings.summary: Digest canonicalization is not fixed for every generic bundle content entry.
findings.adversarial_construction: Supply a content_digest for a generic record whose content has multiple possible serializations and no record-level canonicalization declaration.
findings.consequence: Independent implementations can disagree on digest validity without violating the current entry schema.

findings.summary: Optional A2A-shaped coverage remains optional and does not block the two-transport minimum.
findings.adversarial_construction: Use local/native and MCP-shaped transport profiles without an A2A fixture.
findings.consequence: No current inconsistency; first harness scope remains narrower than the optional future coverage.
